rows.check: 2.4-mathematics (the new _invert: derivation and domain)
rows.location: tools/fetch_data.py _invert (lines 203-222 at 7254468); domain: _PLAIN_NUMBER = -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? (line 141)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 0b7849f (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Derivation checked line by line. x = Fraction(value), exact; x = 0 is refused (DataError). inv = 1/|x| = q/p exactly, with p = numerator, q = denominator of |x|. lead0 = len(str(q)) - len(str(p)); if q in [10^(n1-1), 10^n1) and p in [10^(n2-1), 10^n2) then inv in (10^(n1-n2-1), 10^(n1-n2+1)), so floor(log10 inv) is lead0-1 or lead0. The branch 'if inv < 10**lead0: lead = lead0-1' therefore gives 10^lead <= inv < 10^(lead+1) (verified in the proof and by the 264,470-input check, which exercises both branches). y = inv/10^(lead-7) lies in [10^7, 10^8); round(y) (Fraction.__round__, half to even, exact) gives digits in [10^7, 10^8]; digits = 10^8 happens only when y >= 10^8 - 1/2, and then digits, lead = 10^7, lead+1 gives 10^(lead+1) exactly, matching the rule 9.99999996 -> 10.000000. Output Decimal(digits).scaleb(lead-7) is exact and plain (:f). Sign: the sign of x is restored; abs() makes lead well defined for negative x. Domain: every accepted value is a terminating decimal, so the only inputs whose inverse is an exact 9-digit tie are x = 0.4096 x 10^-k (the ties 2.44140625 x 10^k), as shown in r16-equiv-I03. Result: the derivation is correct for every plain decimal input.
